utility.notes: WestLight Energy's own announcement confirms PG&E's continued role: 'WestLight Energy customers see a new line item on their PG&E bill for WestLight Energy's service, along with a corresponding generation credit from PG&E for the energy supply PG&E previously provided.' PG&E is the underlying transmission/distribution/billing utility; WestLight Energy is a separate default generation supplier — see generation_supplier.

value.name: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) - ECOplus (default)
value.notes: WestLight Energy's own announcement states it 'is a joint powers authority of the 20 cities in San Mateo County, and the county itself' serving 'all electric customers in San Mateo County' — the City of San Mateo is one of these 20 member cities. Default product: 'WestLight Energy customers are automatically enrolled in ECOplus, a 50% renewable energy supply that is cleaner and greener than PG&E.' The organization rebranded from Peninsula Clean Energy to WestLight Energy; the source URL itself redirected from peninsulacleanenergy.com to westlightenergy.org, confirming the rebrand.

county.notes: WestLight Energy's own page confirms San Mateo is one of the '20 cities in San Mateo County' it serves as a joint powers authority.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes San Mateo/San Mateo County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

value.name: Completed eligibility checklist for expedited review
Completed standard electrical plan (available on the City's website)
Roof Plan (roof configuration, panel placement, fire-safety access points/pathways, system classification, label locations)

required_documents.notes: From San Mateo Municipal Code Section 23.46.050 (Submittal Requirements). Applicants qualifying under SB 379 may alternatively use the automated SolarAPP+ portal in lieu of these standard/paper submittals.

value: Building Official first verifies the submission is complete and code-compliant; a written correction notice is issued if deficiencies exist
Only one inspection is required and performed by the Building Division for eligible expedited-review systems
An inspection is scheduled within two business days of a request, with a two-hour inspection window
If the system fails the initial inspection, a subsequent inspection is authorized but need not follow the same scheduling requirements

timeline_days.notes: San Mateo Municipal Code Chapter 23.46 (Sections 23.46.040 and 23.46.070, directly read this session) states inspections are scheduled within 2 business days of a request, but no section found states an overall application-to-permit-issuance timeline distinct from that inspection-scheduling window — left null rather than substituting the inspection-scheduling figure for a permit-review timeline, which is a different concept.

value.program_or_pathway: Small Residential Rooftop Solar Energy Systems (San Mateo Municipal Code Ch. 23.46) / SolarAPP+ per SB 379
other_conditions: Solar panel array may not exceed the maximum legal building height as defined by the City
System must conform to all applicable state fire, structural, electrical, and building codes and state/local health and safety standards

eligibility_constraints.notes: Directly quoted from Municipal Code Section 23.46.020(g)'s definition of 'small residential rooftop solar energy system': 'no larger than 10 kilowatts alternating current nameplate rating of 30 kilowatts thermal' and 'installed on a single or duplex family dwelling.'
